ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n12/r1.claim: The passage closes the account of God's favors by returning to man's intellectual potential, his greatest gift, linked with verses 4, 8, and 14 and the creation allegory in 2:30-33.
ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n12/r1.anchor: the theme introduced in verse 4 and alluded to, indirectly, in the last sentence of verse 8 as well as in verse 14:namely, the consideration of man's intellectual potential - the greatest of all the gifts bestowed upon him by God

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r9.claim: The phrase about further signs indicates that earth holds additional secrets unknown to people at the time, later discoverable through physical geography, geology, and biology.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r9.anchor: “Daha nice işaretler koydu” ifadesinden yeryüzünün, o dönem insanlarının henüz bilmedikleri, zamanla fizikî coğrafya, jeoloji, biyoloji gibi bilimlerin gelişmesiyle keşfedilecek olan daha başka sırlar taşıdığına işaret edilmektedir.

BURSEVI:v5p16/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p16/r1.claim: An anonymous maxim urges taking the road despite its turns, living in town despite hardship, and marrying a virgin even if barren; Bursevī glosses بارت as barren, ruined, and worthless.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم خذوا الطريق ولو دارت واسكنوا المدن ولو جارت وتزوجوا البكر ولو بارت

BURSEVI:v5p16/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p16/r2.claim: Daytime travelers use landmarks such as mountains, plains, water, trees, and wind to find their way.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r2.anchor: وجعل فيها معالم يستدل بها السابلة وهي القوم المختلفة على الطريق بالنهار من جبل وسهل ومياه وأشجار وريح

BURSEVI:v5p16/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r3.speaker: الإمام
BURSEVI:v5p16/r3.claim: The Imam observed travelers sniffing the soil and identifying roads through its smell.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r3.anchor: قال الإمام : رأيت جماعة يشمون التراب وبواسطة ذلك الشم يتعرفون الطرقات

BURSEVI:v5p16/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p16/r4.claim: At night in deserts and seas, travelers navigate by stars where no other landmark is available.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r4.anchor: بالليل في البراري والبحار حيث لا علامة غيره

BURSEVI:v5p16/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p16/r5.claim: The pronoun may address Quraysh, famed for trade travel and star navigation; the fronted star and inserted pronoun restrict the guidance and make gratitude especially incumbent.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r5.anchor: ولعل الضمير لقريش فإنهم كانوا كثيري التردد للتجارة مشهورين بالاهتداء بالنجوم في أسفارهم وصرف النظم عن سنن الخطاب

BURSEVI:v5p16/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p16/r6.claim: النجم may mean stars generally or the Pleiades, the two guards, Banāt Naʿsh, and al-Jady; these circumpolar stars show direction, while Suhayl is faint and tested companions’ eyesight.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r6.anchor: والمراد بالنجم الجنس أو هو الثريا والفرقدان وبنات نعش والجدي وذلك لأنها تعلم بها الجهات ليلا

BURSEVI:v5p16/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v5p16/r7.claim: ʿUmar permits learning enough astronomy to navigate roads and determine the direction of prayer, then advises studying genealogy to maintain kinship.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r7.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه : تعلموا من النجوم ما تهتدون به في طرقكم وقبلتكم

BURSEVI:v5p16/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r8.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v5p16/r8.claim: A report names the prophet Idrīs as the first to study the stars and calculation.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r8.anchor: قيل : أول من نظر في النجوم والحساب إدريس النبي عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v5p16/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r9.speaker: بعض السلف
BURSEVI:v5p16/r9.claim: Some early authorities classify the sciences as jurisprudence for religion, medicine for bodies, astronomy for times, and grammar for the tongue.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r9.anchor: قال بعض السلف : العلوم أربعة : الفقه للأديان والطب للأبدان والنجوم للأزمان والنحو للسان

BURSEVI:v5p16/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r10.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v5p16/r10.claim: A prophetic saying warns that taking knowledge from astrology is taking a branch of sorcery.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r10.anchor: وأما قوله عليه السلام : "من اقتبس علما من النجوم اقتبس شعبة من السحر"

BURSEVI:v5p16/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r11.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v5p16/r11.claim: Al-Ḥāfiẓ explains the prohibited astrology as claims to foretell future events from planetary motions and conjunctions, knowledge reserved to God.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r11.anchor: قال الحافظ : المنهي عنه من علم النجوم هو ما يدعيه أهلها من معرفة الحوادث الآتية

BURSEVI:v5p16/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p16/r12.claim: Astrologers predicted destructive winds from a rare conjunction in 581 AH, but no wind came, exposing the failure of such forecasts.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r12.anchor: حكي أنه لما وقع قران الكواكب السبعة في دقيقة من الدرجة الثالثة من الميزان سنة إحدى وثمانين وخمسمائة

BURSEVI:v5p16/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p16/r13.speaker: تلميذ من شيخه
BURSEVI:v5p16/r13.claim: A departing student was advised to avoid astrologers to escape grief and doctors to preserve the pleasure of eating.
BURSEVI:v5p16/r13.anchor: فقال : إن أردت أن لا تحزن أبدا فلا تصحب منجما وإن أردت أن تبقي لذة فمك

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Classical Arabic leaves recoverable components unspoken in the constructions about paths and landmarks; the translation supplies the omitted wording.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Some components are suppressed here in accordance with a linguistic style of classical Arabic. They have been expressed in the translation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Landmarks help people recognize paths and find their way.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: to recognize these paths, He has fixed various landmarks so that people can assess them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Stars guide desert travellers at night and also help measure time.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The stars that glow in the night sky guide those who travel in the deserts and also are a means of measuring time.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: These created blessings imply that worship is due to God rather than deities that created none of them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: should He be worshipped or other deities who have not created any of these things?

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says the signs are mountains.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي في قوله تعالى ﴿ وعلامات ﴾ قال الجبال

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r2.claim: Qatada says the signs are stars.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r2.anchor: قال عبد الرازق قال معمر وقال قتادة النجوم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam transmits a report, which he understood as prophetic, describing creations that overcome one another until God creates death and says that He prevails over it; it also says mercy overcomes wrath and charity extinguishes sin.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#4/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم لا أعلمه إلا رفعه قال لم يخلق الله خلقا وقد خلق ما يغلبه خلق رحمته تغلب غضبه وخلق الصدقة تطفىء الخطيئة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī defines landmarks as features travelers use for orientation, such as mountains and plains; Abū Ḥayyān says this is also Ibn ʿAbbās’s explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r1.anchor: وعلامات هي معالم الطرق، وكل ما يستدل به السابلة من جبل وسهل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī says he saw groups identify roads by smelling the soil.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: ورأيت جماعة يتعرفون الطرقات بشم التراب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r3.speaker: ابن عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā defines a sign as a form that communicates an intended meaning through writing, speech, gesture, or appearance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عيسى: العلامة صورة يعلم بها ما يراد من خط أو لفظ أو إشارة أو هيئة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah treats “landmarks” as a verbal-noun-like accusative: these things serve as lessons and indications along every route, and mountains, rivers, and roads can all guide.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وعلامات نصب كالمصدر أي: فعل هذه الأشياء لعلكم تعتبرون بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r5.speaker: ابن الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Kalbī identifies the landmarks as mountains.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r6.speaker: النخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r6.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī and Mujāhid identify the landmarks as stars.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r7.claim: An unusual explanation calls the landmarks long, thin, snake-like fish in the Indian Ocean; their appearance signals arrival in India and safety on the route from Yemen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r7.anchor: وأغرب ما فسرت به العلامات أنها حيتان طوال رقاق كالحيات في ألوانها وحركاتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r8.claim: Most readers have al-najm as a generic collective noun; Ibn Waththāb and al-Ḥasan read it with dammah, and authorities transmit these forms from ʿĀṣim’s circle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وبالنجم، على أنه اسم جنس، ويؤيد ذلك قراءة ابن وثاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r9.claim: The vocalized form is best taken as a collective plural, like saqf/saquf and rahn/ruhun, rather than as “stars” with a deleted wāw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r9.anchor: وجعله مما جمع على فعل أولى من حمله على أنه أراد النجوم، فحذف الواو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r10.speaker: ابن عصفور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṣfūr says using the singular al-najm for stars is forced by poetic necessity and cites a verse about the star’s disappearance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r10.anchor: إلا أن ابن عصفور ذكر أن قولهم: النجم من ضرورة الشعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r11.claim: A second poem uses “throats” in the singular-like hilaqīm form to mean plural throats, offered as a parallel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r11.anchor: مثل قوله: حتى إذا ابتلت حلاقيم الحلق يريد: الحلوق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r12.claim: The sukūn in the reading is explained either as a lightened pronunciation or as a dialect form.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r13.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r13.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the star with the Pleiades, the two Firqads, Banāt Naʿsh, and al-Jady; al-Farrāʾ identifies it as al-Jady and the two Firqads.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r13.anchor: وعن السدي: هو الثريا، والفرقدان، وبنات نعش، والجدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r14.claim: Al-Jady here is the seventh of the smaller Banāt Naʿsh, while the two Firqads are its first two stars; this is distinct from al-Jady as a lunar station.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r14.anchor: قيل: والجدي هو السابع من بنات نعش الصغرى، والفرقدان الأولان منها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports asking the Prophet about “by the star,” and the Prophet identified it as al-Jady.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514#2/r15.anchor: وفي الحديث عن ابن عباس أنه سأل الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قوله: وبالنجم، فقل: «هو الجدي»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the star supplies the direction for the qibla and guides travelers on land and sea.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: عليه قبلتكم، وبه تهتدون في بركم وبحركم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r2.claim: An unnamed view identifies the star as the pole star, which does not move.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو القطب الذي لا يجري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r3.claim: Another view identifies the star as the Pleiades.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r4.claim: An anonymous poem describes the rising star helping travelers find crossings of the Euphrates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r4.anchor: إذا طلب الجوزاء والنجم طالع ... فكل مخاضات الفرات معابر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r5.claim: A second poem links the rising Pleiades with grass being bent and harvested.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r5.anchor: حتى إذا ما استقل النجم في غلس ... وغودر البقل ملوى ومحصود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r6.claim: The third-person pronoun shifts from direct address to Quraysh, who navigated by stars and therefore had special grounds for gratitude and reflection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r6.anchor: كان الضمير النعت به إلى قريش إذ كان لهم اهتداء بالنجوم في مسايرهم، وكان لهم بذلك علم لم يكن لغيرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r7.claim: The preposed phrase receives emphasis and serves the verse ending; al-Zamakhshari paraphrases it as guidance by the star in particular.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p515/r7.anchor: وقدم المجرور على ما يتعلق به اعتناء ولأجل الفاصلة. والزمخشري على عادته كأنه قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r1.claim: Signs are landmarks travelers use, such as mountains, water sources, and even the smell of soil, which can show whether a route is frequented; masafa is connected to smelling.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r1.anchor: معالم يستدل بها السابلة من نحو جبل ومنهل ورائحة تراب فقد حكى أن من الناس من يشم التراب

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the signs as landmarks along roads by day.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وغيره عن ابن عباس أنها معالم الطرق بالنهار

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the signs as mountains.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the signs as stars.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r5.speaker: ابن عيسى
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r5.claim: Ibn Isa interprets signs broadly as anything that conveys what is intended, including writing, words, gestures, or appearance.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عيسى : المراد منها الأمور التي يعلم بها ما يراد من خط أو لفظ أو إشارة أو هيئة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r6.claim: The author favors the initial interpretation as landmarks and calls the most unusual alternative a far-fetched report of long, thin, snake-like fish in the Indian Sea whose appearance signals reaching India and safety.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#2/r6.anchor: والظاهر ما ذكر أولا وأغرب ما فسرت به وأبعده أن المراد منها حيتان طوال رقاق كالحيات

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r1.claim: Travelers are guided by stars at night on land and sea; the generic star includes al-khunnas and other stars that guide the way.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r1.anchor: بالليل في البر والبحر والمراد بالنجم الجنس فبش ما الخنس وغيرها مما يهتدى به

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r2.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r2.claim: Al-Suddi restricts the star to the Pleiades, the two Farqads, Banat Naʿsh, and al-Jady.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r2.anchor: وعن السدي تخصيص ذلك بالثريا والفرقدين وبنات نعش والجدي

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r3.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r3.claim: Al-Farra restricts it to al-Jady and the two Farqads.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r4.claim: Some identify it with the Pleiades because al-najm conventionally names them, citing a report that when the star rises seasonal affliction lifts.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r4.anchor: وعن بعضهم أنه الثريا فإنه علم بالغلبة لها ففي الحديث إذا طلح النجم ارتفعت العاهة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas asked the Prophet, who answered that the star is al-Jady; if this report is sound, the author says it should not be set aside.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه سأل النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن ذلك فقال : هو الجدي ولو صح هذا لا يعدل عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r6.claim: Al-Jady means the Jady of the Farqads; al-Maghrib gives its standard pronunciation, while astrologers use a diminutive to distinguish it from the zodiac sign, though another view calls that pronunciation dialectal.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r6.anchor: والجدي هو جدي الفرقد وهو على ما في المغرب بفتح الجيم وسكون الدال والمنجمون يصغرونه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r7.speaker: الحسن وابن وثاب
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r7.claim: Al-Hasan reads the word with two dammas and Ibn Waththab with damma then sukun; both are plural forms, like سقف and رهن, and the sukun is either for ease or dialect.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r7.anchor: عن الحسن أنه قرأ والنجم ( بضمتين ) وعن ابن وثاب أنه قرأ بضم فسكون

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r8.claim: The author prefers explaining the readings as a plural on the faʿul pattern over claiming that the waw was deleted from the plural nujum.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r8.anchor: والقول بأن ذلك جمع على فعل أولى مما قيل : إن أصله النجوم فحذفت الواو

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r9.speaker: ابن عصفور
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r9.claim: Ibn Asfur says using singular al-najm is forced by poetic meter, citing a line about returning to water when the star disappears; the author compares another poetic omission.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r9.anchor: وزعم ابن عصفور أن قولهم : النجم من ضرورة الشعر وأنشد : إن الذي قضى بذا قاض حكم أن يرد الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r10.claim: The pronoun may refer to all travelers in the preceding address, with a shift in person, fronting for cadence, and a detached pronoun for emphasis; or it singles out Quraysh, famed for trade journeys and navigation by stars.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r10.anchor: والضمير يحتمل أن يكون عاما لكل سالك في البر والبحر من المخاطبين فيما تقدم وتغيير التعبير للالتفات

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r11.claim: If the pronoun singles out Quraysh, their special familiarity with star navigation makes considering the sign and thanking God through tawhid especially binding on them.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r11.anchor: فالإعتبار بذلك والشكر عليه بالتوحيد ألزم لهم وأوجب عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r12.claim: Some take the verse as a basis for learning stars to determine times, the qibla, and routes; learning what enables these is permissible.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r12.anchor: وجعل بعضهم الآية أصلا لمراعاة النجوم لمعرفة الأوقات والقبلة والطرق فلا بأس بتعلم ما يفيد تلك المعرفة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r13.speaker: أبو العباس أحمد بن البناء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r13.claim: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn al-Banna says exact qibla determination from stars is difficult or impossible: a star's position over Mecca does not transfer to another city, and al-Jady's shoulder or side position works only on a particular, uncertain meridian.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r13.anchor: كما أفاده العلامة الرباني أبو العباس أحمد بن البناء لأنه إن اعتبر ذلك بما يسامت رؤس أهل مكة من النجوم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r14.claim: Using the midsummer sun at local zenith fails because two distant cities do not share that zenith at the same time; treating Mecca's zenith as the reference requires uncertain longitude data.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r14.anchor: وقول من قال : إن ذلك يعرف بجعل المصلي مثلا الشمس بين عينيه إذا استوت في كبد السماء أطول يوم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r15.speaker: أبو العباس أحمد بن البناء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r15.claim: Even Indian-circle methods cannot determine the qibla exactly because they rely on uncertain longitudes and latitudes; worshippers need only seek the direction, which stars and other means can establish.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116#3/r15.anchor: بل قال قدس سره : إن معرفة ذلك على التحقيق بما يذكرونه من الدائرة الهندية ونحوها متعذر أيضا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r4.claim: The signs are landmarks along roads; one view ends the clause there and begins a new clause about the stars.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r4.anchor: {وعلامات} يعني: معالم الطرق. قال بعضهم: هاهنا تم الكلام ثم ابتدأ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب، الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b and al-Kalbi say the signs are mountains, landmarks by day, while stars guide at night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r5.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب، والكلبي: أراد بالعلامات الجبال، فالجبال تكون علامات النهار، والنجوم علامات الليل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r6.claim: Mujahid takes all the signs to be stars: some serve as landmarks and some guide travelers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أراد بالكل النجوم، منها ما يكون علامات ومنها ما يهتدون به.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r7.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r7.claim: Al-Suddi names the Pleiades, Banat Na'sh, the two Farqads, and al-Judayy as stars used to find roads and the qibla.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r7.anchor: قال السدي: أراد بالنجم، الثريا، وبنات نعش، والفرقدين، والجدي، يهتدى بها إلى الطرق والقبلة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r8.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r8.claim: Qatada says stars were created as heaven's adornment, road markers, and missiles against devils; other claimed purposes exceed knowledge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: إنما خلق الله النجوم لثلاثة أشياء: لتكون زينة للسماء، ومعالم للطرق، ورجوما للشياطين

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r5.claim: Landmarks include features such as mountains, plains, and winds by which travelers navigate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r5.anchor: معالم يستدل بها السابلة من جبل وسهل وريح ونحو ذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r6.claim: The star guides travelers by night on land and sea, and the singular may mean the generic class; a plural reading supports that.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r6.anchor: بالليل في البراري والبحار، والمراد بالنجم الجنس

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r7.claim: Alternatively, the star means al-Thurayyā, the two al-Farqadān, Banāt Naʿsh, or al-Jady.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r7.anchor: وقيل الثريا والفرقدان وبنات نعش والجدي

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r8.claim: The pronoun may refer to Quraysh, known for frequent commercial journeys and skilled star navigation; the shifted address, fronted star, and emphatic pronoun focus on their special guidance and obligation to reflect and give thanks.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r8.anchor: ولعل الضمير لقريش لأنهم كانوا كثيري الأسفار للتجارة مشهورين بالاهتداء في مسايرهم بالنجوم

SULAMI:v1p363#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p363#4/r1.speaker: المالكي
SULAMI:v1p363#4/r1.claim: Guidance has landmarks that lead to its destination, and the stars of gnosis guide the traveler to the end; God alone is the guide to Himself, with no created sign or route to Him apart from Him, and arrival or severance follows prior decree.
SULAMI:v1p363#4/r1.anchor: قال المالكي : طريق الهداية له أعلام فمن استدل بالأعلام بلغ إلى محل الهدى وكوشف عن معدن النجوى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r3.claim: Signs include mountains and other markers; a sign is a perceptible form by which meaning is known, whether through writing, speech, gesture, or shape, and it may be conventional or demonstrative.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r3.anchor: جمع علامة وهي صورة يعلم بها المعنى من خط , أو لفظ أو إشارة أو هيئة , وقد تكون علامة وضعية , وقد تكون برهانية

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r4.claim: Guidance by stars is the most useful, comprehensive, and clear form of guidance on land and sea, by day and night.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r4.anchor: ولما كانت الدلالة بالنجم أنفع الدلالات وأعمها وأوضحها برا وبحرا ليلا ونهارا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r5.claim: The shift to third person broadens the statement to all earth's inhabitants, especially the first addressees Quraysh and then all Arabs, who knew the stars exceptionally well.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r5.anchor: لإفهام العموم لئلا يظن أن المخاطب مخصوص , وأن الأمر لا يتعداه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r6.claim: Fronting the phrase about the star signals that other forms of guidance rank below it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r6.anchor: وقدم الجار تنبيها على أن دلالة غيره بالنسبة إليه سافلة

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r7.claim: The paths are roads and the signs are stars.
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وسبلا} قال: طرقا {وعلامات} قال: هي النجوم

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r8.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {وعلامات} قال: أنهار الجبال

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r9.speaker: الكلبي
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r9.anchor: عن الكلبي في قوله: {وعلامات} قال: الجبال

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r10.claim: Daytime signs are landmarks of roads, while stars guide people at night.
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وعلامات} يعني معالم الطرق بالنهار {وبالنجم هم يهتدون} يعني بالليل

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r11.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r11.claim: The signs are markers in the sky, and stars guide travelers at sea.
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r11.anchor: عن إبراهيم {وعلامات} قال: هي الاعلام التي في السماء {وبالنجم هم يهتدون} قال: يهتدون به في البحر

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r12.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r12.claim: Some of the signs serve as markers, while some are used for guidance.
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r12.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {وعلامات وبالنجم هم يهتدون} قال: منها ما يكون علامة ومنها ما يهتدى به

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r13.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r13.claim: Mujahid saw no harm in learning the moon's stations.
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r13.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه كان لا يرى بأسا أن يتعلم الرجل منازل القمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r1.claim: The passage shifts to evidence and gratitude for great creatures on Earth’s surface that benefit people; calling their creation ‘casting’ pictures them as additions placed on a completed Earth, perhaps created later.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r1.anchor: انتقال إلى الاستدلال والامتنان بما على سطح الأرض من المخلوقات العظيمة التي في وجودها لطف بالإنسان . وهذه المخلوقات لما كانت مجعولة كالتكملة للأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur suggests mountains may have emerged through great seismic disturbances and rivers through heavy rain; roads and markers clearly came later, making all four resemble objects cast onto something complete.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r2.anchor: ولعل خلقها كان متأخرا عن خلق الأرض ، إذ لعل الجبال انبثقت باضطرابات أرضية كالزلزال العظيم ثم حدثت الأنهار بتهاطل الأمطار .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r3.claim: He also proposes that mountains formed from debris cast off by celestial bodies and rain formed rivers; ‘casting’ fits these naturally and extends to routes and markers by generalization, as in 54:25 for giving revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r3.anchor: ولعل أصل تكوين الجبال كان من شظايا رمت بها الكواكب فصادفت سطح الأرض ، كما أن الأمطار تهاطلت فكونت الأنهار ؛ فيكون تشبيه حصول هذين بالإلقاء بينا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r9.claim: Markers are signs God inspires people to establish or recognize so travelers can identify distances and safe land and sea routes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r9.anchor: والعلامات : الأمارات التي ألهم الله الناس أن يضعوها أو يتعارفوها لتكون دلالة على المسافات والمسالك المأمونة في البر والبحر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r10.claim: The star clause coordinates with the creation clause but means that God guided people by stars; this is a night-travel blessing because routes and markers guide by day, while stars help travelers in dark and confusing conditions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r10.anchor: وجملة { وبالنجم هم يهتدون } معطوفة على جملة { وألقى في الأرض رواسي } ، لأنها في معنى : وهداكم بالنجم فأنتم تهتدون به . وهذه منة بالاهتداء في الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r11.claim: Sailors especially rely on stars because they cannot moor every night and must sail at night; fronting ‘by the star’ and ‘they’ marks the importance of this guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r11.anchor: وأخص من يهتدي بها البحارة لأنهم لا يستطيعون الإرساء في كل ليلة فهم مضطرون إلى السير ليلا ، وهي هداية عظيمة في وقت ارتباك الطريق على السائر ، ولذلك قدم المتعلق

FARRA:v2p97/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p97/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p97/r6.claim: The stars used for navigation are identified as al-Jady and al-Farqadān.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r1.claim: ʿAlāmāt is an accusative of purpose: God made these things so people would learn from them; the signs guide in every route, including mountains, rivers, and roads.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r1.anchor: علامات نصب على المصدر، أي فعل هذه الأشياء لعلكم تعتبرون بها وعلامات أي عبرة وإعلاما في كل سلوك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r2.speaker: ابن الكلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Kalbī says the signs are mountains.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r3.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and Mujāhid identify the signs as stars.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the signs are landmarks along roads by day, while stars guide at night.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «العلامات» معالم الطرق بالنهار، والنجوم هداية الليل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r5.claim: If the clause is read independently of what precedes it, every indicator counts as a sign; Ibn Atiyya favors Ibn ʿAbbās because his account is broad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r5.anchor: والصواب إذا قدرنا الكلام غير معلق بما قبله أن اللفظة تعم هذا وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r6.speaker: أبو القاضي محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya’s father heard an eastern scholar describe long, slender, twisting, brightly colored fish in the Indian Ocean as ‘signs’ that mark arrival and safe passage to India; some identified them with this verse’s signs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r6.anchor: وحدثني أبي رضي الله عنه أنه سمع بعض أهل العلم بالمشرق يقول: إن في بحر الهند الذي يجرى فيه من اليمن إلى الهند حيتانا طوالا رقاقا كالحيات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r7.speaker: أبي القاضي محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya’s father says numerous people who saw those sea signs told him about them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r7.anchor: قال أبي رضي الله عنه: وأما من شاهد تلك العلامات في البحر المذكور وعاينها فحدثني منهم عدد كثير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r8.claim: The majority read al-najm as a collective singular, ‘the star.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «وبالنجم» على أنه اسم الجنس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r9.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r9.claim: Yaḥyā b. Waththāb reads the nūn with ḍamma and the jīm quiescent, a lightened form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب «وبالنجم» بضم النون والجيم ساكنة على التخفيف من ضمها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the nūn with ḍamma as a plural form, comparable to alternative forms of ‘roof’ and ‘pledge.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «وبالنجم» بضم النون وذلك جمع، كسقف وسقف، ورهن ورهن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r11.claim: The reading may instead mean ‘by the stars,’ with the wāw omitted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p384#2/r11.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد وبالنجوم، فحذفت الواو

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r1.claim: Landmarks such as great mountains and small hills guide travelers on land and sea when they lose their way by day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r1.anchor: دلائل من جبال كبار وآكام صغار، ونحو ذلك، يستدل بها المسافرون برا وبحرا إذا ضلوا الطريق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the stars guide people in the darkness of night.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r2.anchor: أي: في ظلام الليل، قاله ابن عباس.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r3.claim: Malik transmits the explanation that the landmarks are the stars, which are the mountains.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p564/r3.anchor: وعن مالك في قوله: {وعلامات} يقولون: النجوم، وهي الجبال.

JISHUMI:v6p4010/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r1.claim: The verses point to God's great blessings in the animals, trees, fruits, and other things He created and subjected for people's benefit.
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r1.anchor: تدل الآية على عظيم نعمه تعالى بما خلق وسخر من أنواع الحيوان والأشجار والثمار وغير ذلك. وتدل على أنه خلق جميع ذلك لمنافع خلقه

JISHUMI:v6p4010/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r2.claim: God intends people to reflect on creation; this makes reasoning obligatory and undermines uncritical imitation. Reflection is an act of people, so commands and encouragement to reflect are sound.
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r2.anchor: وتدل على أنه أراد من خلقه التفكر فيه فيوجب النظر ويفسد التقليد. وتدل على أن النظر والتفكر فعل العبد ليصح الأمر به، والبعث عليه

JISHUMI:v6p4010/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r7.claim: A sign is a form by which a meaning is known, whether through writing, speech, a gesture, or another means.
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r7.anchor: والعلامة صورة يعلم بها المعنى من خط أو لفظ أو اشارة أو غيرها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r8.claim: The signs are landmarks for daytime travel, while stars guide at night.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r8.anchor: أحدها : أنها معالم الطريق بالنهار , وبالنجوم يهتدون بالليل , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والنخعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r9.claim: The signs are also stars, since some stars serve as guides.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r9.anchor: الثاني : أنها النجوم أيضا لأن من النجوم ما يهتدي بها , قاله مجاهد وقتادة والنخعي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r10.claim: A third interpretation of the signs is mountains.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r11.claim: ‘The star’ may be a collective singular referring to the fixed stars as a class.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r11.anchor: أحدهما : أنه جمع النجوم الثابتة , فعبر عنها بالنجم الواحد إشارة إلى الجنس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r12.claim: Alternatively, it is the Jady alone, since it is the most fixed star at its center.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r12.anchor: الثاني : أنه الجدي وحده لأنه أثبت النجوم كلها في مركزه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r13.claim: The stars may guide travelers on all journeys, according to the majority.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r13.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أراد الاهتداء بها في جميع الأسفار , قاله الجمهور .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r14.claim: Alternatively, they guide people in determining the direction of prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r14.anchor: الثاني : أنه أراد الاهتداء به في القبلة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas asked the Prophet about the verse; the Prophet identified the star as Jady, the qibla, and a guide on land and sea.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p181#2/r15.anchor: قال ابن عباس : سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قوله تعالى { وبالنجم هم يهتدون } قال ( هو الجدي يا ابن عباس عليه قبلتكم , وبه تهتدون في بركم وبحركم ) .

MUQATIL:16:14-17/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r3.claim: The signs are mountains, as in the cited comparison to mountain-like landmarks.
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r3.anchor:
يعني الجبال، كقوله سبحانه:
كالأعلام
[الرحمن: 14]، يعني الجبال

MUQATIL:16:14-17/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r4.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r4.claim: The stars used for navigation are Banat Na'sh, al-Jady, the two Farqads, and al-Qutb; they stay fixed year-round and, together with mountains, help travelers navigate land and sea.
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل: هي بنات نعش، والجدي، والفرقدان، والقطب، قال: بعينها لأنهن لا يزلن عن أماكنهن شتاء ولا صيفا، يعني بالجبال، والكواكب، وبها يعرفون الطرق في البر والبحر

MUQATIL:16:14-17/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r5.claim: People find their way by the stars, while the linked phrase about not finding a path means not knowing the way.
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r5.anchor:
لا يهتدون سبيلا
[النساء: 98]، يعني لا يعرفون

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r1.claim: The signs are landmarks of roads, including mountains and anything else travelers use for orientation.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r1.anchor: هي معالم الطرق وكل ما يستدل به السابلة من جبل وغير ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r2.claim: The star may mean stars generally or specifically the Pleiades, the two Furqadān, Banāt Naʿsh, and al-Jady.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r2.anchor: المراد بالنجم الجنس أو هو التريا والفرقدان وبنات نعش والجدى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r3.claim: Fronting the star and inserting they emphasizes exclusive guidance; the referent is Quraysh, singled out because they navigate by stars and have exceptional knowledge, making gratitude and reflection especially incumbent.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#2/r3.anchor: كأنه قيل وبالنجم خصوصا هؤلاء خصوصا يهتدون فمن المراد بهم قلت كانه أراد قريشا

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r1.claim: The signs are daytime landmarks on roads; the stars provide guidance at night.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: العلامات معالم الطرق بالنهار

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r3.speaker: ابن وثاب، الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r3.claim: Ibn Waththab reads the word with a different vocalization; al-Hasan raises both consonants, intending the plural stars in a shortened form.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب «وبالنجم». الحسن: بضم النون والجيم جميعا

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r4.claim: A cited verse shows the shortened usage; reading the word with a sukūn can likewise be an ease form, and it may be an unchanged plural like suquf.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r5.claim: He identifies the guiding stars as al-Jady and the two Farqads.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r5.anchor: واختلف في النجوم فقال الفراء: الجدي والفرقدان.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r6.claim: Another view identifies the star as the Pleiades; a poem locates the harvest and bent vegetation at its rising.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r6.anchor: وقيل: الثريا. قال الشاعر: حتى إذا ما استقل النجم في غلس وغودر البقل ملوي ومحصود أي منه ملوي ومنه محصود، وذلك عند طلوع الثريا يكون.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r7.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r7.claim: He says the signs are mountains.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r8.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r8.claim: They identify the signs as stars, noting that some stars guide while others serve only as markers.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هي النجوم لأن من النجوم ما يهتدى بها، ومنها ما يكون علامة لا يهتدى بها وقاله قتادة والنخعي.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r9.claim: One syntactic reading ends the clause after “signs” and begins “by the star”; the other takes both signs and stars as things God made for guidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r9.anchor: وقيل: تم الكلام عند قوله «وعلامات» ثم ابتدأ

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r10.claim: Winds also count among the signs used for guidance.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r11.claim: Most interpreters say the guidance is for journeys; another view says it is for determining the qibla.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r11.anchor: وفي المراد بالاهتداء قولان: أحدهما في الأسفار، وهذا قول الجمهور. الثاني في القبلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r12.claim: In a report from Ibn Abbas, the Prophet identifies the star as al-Jady, which indicates the qibla and guides on land and sea.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r12.anchor: هو الجدي يابن عباس، عليه قبلتكم وبه تهتدون في بركم وبحركم

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r13.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r13.claim: Most stars guide only experts who know their risings, settings, and north–south positions; ordinary people can use the fixed, conspicuous al-Jady and Farqads for land, sea, and qibla orientation.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r13.anchor: وإنما الهدي لكل أحد بالجدي والفرقدين لأنها من النجوم المنحصرة المطالع الظاهرة السمت

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r14.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r14.claim: He gives the practical orientation: place the pole behind the left shoulder, and the direction faced is the relevant direction.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16/r14.anchor: بأن تجعل القطب على ظهر منكبك الأيسر فما استقبلت فهو سمت الجهة

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r1.claim: In response to Ibn Abbas, the Prophet identifies the Najm as al-Jady, by which people find direction on land and sea.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r1.anchor: وسأل ابن عباس رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن النجم فقال: «هو الجدي عليه قبلتكم وبه تهتدون في بركم وبحركم»

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r2.claim: The end of al-Jady is the small Banat Naʿsh, with the pole around which the qibla turns lying between them.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r2.anchor: وذلك أن آخر الجدي بنات نعش الصغرى والقطب الذي تستوي عليه القبلة بينها.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r3.claim: Qurtubi divides qibla orientation into two cases: when the Kaaba is visible, one must face and accurately aim toward it with the whole body.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما أن يراها ويعاينها فيلزمه استقبالها وإصابتها وقصد جهتها بجميع بدنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r4.claim: When the Kaaba is unseen, one must determine its direction by indications such as the sun, moon, stars, and winds.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r4.anchor: والآخر أن تكون الكعبة بحيث لا يراها فيلزمه التوجه نحوها وتلقاءها بالدلائل، وهي الشمس والقمر والنجوم والرياح

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r5.claim: A person able to reason out the direction who prays away from the qibla has not performed a valid prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r5.anchor: ومن غابت عنه وصلى مجتهدا إلى غير ناحيتها وهي ممن يمكنه الاجتهاد فلا صلاة له

QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r6.claim: If the person discovers after praying that the direction was wrong, Qurtubi says to repeat within the prayer time, though it is not obligatory because the duty was performed as commanded.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:16#2/r6.anchor: فإذا صلى مستدلا ثم انكشف له بعد الفراغ من صلاته أنه صلى إلى غير القبلة أعاد إن كان في وقتها، وليس ذلك بواجب عليه لأنه قد أدى فرضه على ما أمر به.

RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r3.claim: Signs are coordinated with mountains, rivers, and paths and mean route markers; these include mountains and winds, and some people identify roads by smelling soil.
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بالعلامات معالم الطرق وهي الأشياء التي بها يهتدي

RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r4.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash says the sentence ends at “signs,” and “by the star they are guided” begins a separate statement; star is then a generic singular.
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r4.anchor: قال الأخفش تم الكلام عند قوله : { وعلامات } وقوله : { وبالنجم هم يهتدون } كلام منفصل

RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r5.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the stars as the Pleiades, the two al-Farqadān, Banāt Naʿsh, and al-Jady.
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r5.anchor: وعن السدي هو الثريا ، والفرقدان ، وبنات نعش ، والجدي

RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads nجم as a plural in two vocalizations, nujum and nujm; the second is a lightened form.
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : { وبالنجم } بضمتين وبضمة فسكون ، وهو جمع نجم

RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r7.claim: Another explanation says the wāw was omitted from the word star for ease of pronunciation.
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : حذف الواو من النجم تخفيفا

RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r8.claim: The address shifts from present listeners about earth's shaking to absent “they” because Quraysh frequently traveled for trade and therefore knew the benefits of star navigation especially well.
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r8.anchor: إن قريشا كانت تكثر أسفارها لطلب المال ، ومن كثرت أسفاره كان علمه بالمنافع الحاصلة من الاهتداء بالنجوم أكثر وأتم

RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r1.claim: Some commentators restrict star guidance to sea travel because the preceding discussion describes the sea.
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r1.anchor: واختلف المفسرون فمنهم من قال قوله : { وبالنجم هم يهتدون } مختص بالبحر

RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r2.claim: Al-Razi prefers guidance for travel on both land and sea, since this is a broader blessing and stars guide in both settings.
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r2.anchor: ومنهم من قال : بل هو مطلق يدخل فيه السير في البر والبحر وهذا القول أولى

RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r3.claim: He accepts the jurists' inference that a traveler unsure of the qibla should use stars and terrestrial signs, since signs that guide routes can also indicate the qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r3.anchor: وذلك صحيح ، لأنه كما يمكن الاهتداء بهذه العلامات في معرفة الطرق والمسالك فكذلك يمكن الاستدلال بها

RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r4.claim: When qibla signs are apparent, one must reason toward the direction most likely to be the qibla; if error becomes clear, repeat because the person was negligent.
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r4.anchor: فإن كانت لائحة وجب أن يجب الاجتهاد ويتوجه إلى حيث غلب على الظن أنه هو القبلة ، فإن تبين الخطأ وجب الإعادة

RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r5.claim: One proposed rule when no signs appear is to choose any direction, since all directions are equal and none can be preferred.
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r5.anchor: أن يكون مخيرا في الصلاة إلى أي جهة شاء لأن الجهات لما تساوت وامتنع الترجيح لم يبق إلا التخيير

RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r6.claim: The other rule is to pray toward every direction, thereby knowing with certainty that the duty has been discharged.
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r6.anchor: أن يصلي إلى جميع الجهات فحينئذ يعلم بيقين أنه خرج عن العهدة

RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r7.claim: He analogizes an unknown missed prayer to making up all five prayers, and rejects the view that only one is due: if all must be performed, all are obligatory.
RAZI-FULL:v20p10/r7.anchor: ومنهم من يقول : الواجب منها واحدة فقط وهذا غلط لأنه لما لزمه أن يفعل الكل كان الكل واجبا

STUDYQURAN:16:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r1.claim: Landmarks by day and stars by night or at sea, like streams, provide guidance across times and places.
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r1.anchor: other landmarks, visible along the roads by day (Q, Ṭ, Z), and the stars, which are visible by night or when at sea (R)

STUDYQURAN:16:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r2.claim: Alāmāt means landmarks, including mountains (Q, Ṭ), roadside springs (Z), and winds (Q), all offering directional guidance.
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r2.anchor: Landmarks translatesʿalāmāt and may include mountains (Q, Ṭ), springs along the road (Z), and winds (Q), all of which can provide directional guidance.

STUDYQURAN:16:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r3.claim: Pre-Islamic nomads knew winds complexly, reflected in Arabic’s rich vocabulary; the Quran refers to some winds elsewhere.
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r3.anchor: Arabs had developed complex knowledge of winds, which is reflected in the rich vocabulary in Arabic for different kinds of winds

STUDYQURAN:16:16/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r4.speaker: Q, Z
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r4.claim: Q and Z say the singular najm can refer to stars as a single category.
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r4.anchor: It may be singular in the Arabic because it is referring to stars as a single category (Q, Z),

STUDYQURAN:16:16/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r5.speaker: Q, Z
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r5.claim: Q and Z also report that najm can refer to a particular star or constellation, such as the Pleiades, Ursa Major or Minor, or the North Star.
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r5.anchor: such as the Pleiades, Ursa Major or Minor, or the North Star (Q, Z).

STUDYQURAN:16:16/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r6.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r6.claim: The Quraysh relied on stars to navigate desert journeys and therefore should have been grateful for this blessing.
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r6.anchor: the Quraysh were dependent on the stars for navigation during their travels in the desert, they should have been particularly grateful for this blessing (Z)

STUDYQURAN:16:16/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r7.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:16:16/r7.claim: For Muslims, natural guidance sources also help find the direction of prayer in unfamiliar territory.

SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r1.claim: وعلامات means that God placed signs in the landscape.
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r1.anchor: و { وعلامات } ، أي: ووضع فيها علامات.

SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r2.claim: The phrase وبالنجم syntactically attaches to يهتدون.
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وبالنجم } متعلق ب " يهتدون ".

SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r3.claim: The common reading has singular النجم, either a particular star such as Polaris or the Pleiades, or a generic star.
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r3.anchor: والعامة على فتح النون وسكون الجيم بالتوحيد فقيل: المراد به كوكب بعينه كالجدي أو الثريا.

SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r4.speaker: ابن وثاب
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r4.claim: He reads النجم with both letters vocalized in ḍamma; the strongest analysis treats it as a straightforward plural.
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب بضمهما، والحسن بضم النون فقط

SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r5.claim: The double-ḍamma form may instead derive from النجوم, with its wāw dropped as in other shortened plurals.
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r5.anchor: والثاني: أن أصله النجوم، وفعل يجمع على فعول نحو: فلس وفلوس، ثم خفف بحذف الواو

SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r6.claim: He compares the dropped long vowel in this form with خيام shortened to خيم.
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r6.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " وقالوا في خيام: خيم، يعني أنه نظيره، من حيث حذفوا منه حرف المد.

SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r7.speaker: ابن عصفور
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r7.claim: He calls النجم a poetic necessity for النجوم and cites a line where the word means the stars.
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عصفور: إن قولهم " النجم من ضرورة الشعر " وأنشد:

SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r8.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r8.claim: A reading with ḍamma on nūn alone is either a lightened version of the double-ḍamma reading or an independent dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب بضمهما، والحسن بضم النون فقط، وعكس بعضهم النقل عنهما.

SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r9.claim: Fronting both the prepositional phrase and subject conveys restriction.
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r9.anchor: وتقديم كل من الجار والمبتدأ يفيد الاختصاص

SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r10.claim: He says the restricted address is aimed at Quraysh, who navigated by stars and had special knowledge, so they owed greater thanks.
SAMIN-DURR:16:16/r10.anchor: قال الزمشخري: " فإن قلت: قوله: { وبالنجم هم يهتدون } مخرج عن سنن الخطاب، مقدم فيه النجم،

TAB-FULL:v14p192/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r1.claim: The signs are daytime landmarks along routes, while stars guide travelers at night.
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وعلامات، وبالنجم هم يهتدون} [النحل: 16] " يعني بالعلامات: معالم الطرق بالنهار، وبالنجم هم يهتدون بالليل "

TAB-FULL:v14p192/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r2.claim: Some stars serve as signs, while others are used for guidance.
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم: {وعلامات وبالنجم هم يهتدون} [النحل: 16] قال: «منها ما يكون علامات، ومنها ما يهتدون به»

TAB-FULL:v14p192/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r3.claim: Some stars serve as markers, while others are used to find the way.
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وعلامات وبالنجم هم يهتدون} [النحل: 16] قال: «منها ما يكون علامة، ومنها ما يهتدى به»

TAB-FULL:v14p192/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r4.claim: He identifies the signs as stars, created to adorn the sky, guide people, and stone devils; seeking other purposes is baseless and ignorant.
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وعلامات وبالنجم هم يهتدون} [النحل: 16] " والعلامات: النجوم، وإن الله تبارك وتعالى إنما خلق هذه النجوم لثلاث خصلات

TAB-FULL:v14p192/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r5.speaker: الكلبي
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r5.claim: He identifies the signs as mountains.

TAB-FULL:v14p192/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r6.claim: Trodden roads themselves indicate the intended direction; roads, mountains, and stars can all count as signs used to find routes.
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r6.anchor: والطرق المسبولة: الموطوءة، علامة للناحية المقصودة، والجبال علامات يهتدي بهن

TAB-FULL:v14p192/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r7.claim: Because night guidance is separately named, he prefers Ibn Abbas's daytime road markers and identifies the night stars as al-Jadī and al-Farqadān, used by travelers.
TAB-FULL:v14p192/r7.anchor: فالواجب أن يكون القول في ذلك ما قاله ابن عباس في الخبر الذي رويناه عن عطية عنه، وهو أن العلامات معالم الطرق

TABATABAI:16:14-16/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r6.claim: Signs are indicators of things hidden from the senses and include natural or conventional landmarks, markers, languages, gestures, and lines.
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r6.anchor: أي وجعل علامات تستدلون بها على الأشياء الغائبة عن الحس وهي كل آية وأمارة طبيعية أو وضعية تدل على مدلولها ومنها الشواخص والنصب واللغات والإشارات والخطوط وغيرها.

TABATABAI:16:14-16/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r7.claim: People navigate by stars; the shift from direct address to third person likely avoids repeating the second-person form of 'you find guidance' in the prior verses.
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r7.anchor: ولعل الالتفات فيه من الخطاب إلى الغيبة للتحرز عن تكرار { تهتدون } بصيغة الخطاب في آخر الآيتين.

TABATABAI:16:14-16/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r8.claim: Although the spiritual guidance verse would seem more naturally placed after the signs for physical navigation, its current placement avoids confusion and an apparent contradiction.
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r8.anchor: أن يوضع بعد هذه الآية أعني قوله { وبالنجم هم يهتدون } المتعرضة هي وما قبلها للهداية الصورية

TABATABAI:16:1-21#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:1-21#5/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله
TABATABAI:16:1-21#5/r4.claim: The Prophet identifies the star as al-Jady, a star used by travelers on land and sea because the qibla's orientation does not rotate around it; the author says the report is also transmitted from al-Sadiq.
TABATABAI:16:1-21#5/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله { وبالنجم هم يهتدون } قال هو الجدي

TABATABAI:16:1-21#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:1-21#5/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:16:1-21#5/r5.claim: The star symbolizes the Messenger and the signs symbolize the Imams; the author treats this as inner meaning, supported by the report that the Prophet is the star and the Ahl al-Bayt are signs and protection for earth.
TABATABAI:16:1-21#5/r5.anchor: سمعت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام يقول { وعلامات وبالنجم هم يهتدون } قال النجم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والعلامات الأئمة عليهم السلام.

ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r1.claim: The singular najm and plural nujūm have the same sense, as ‘a dirham’ and ‘dirhams’ can both describe many coins in people’s hands.
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r1.anchor: كما تقول: كثر الدرهم في أيدي الناس وكثرت الدراهم،

ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r2.claim: God created stars to adorn the lowest heaven, to stone devils, to guide travelers, and to mark years and reckoning.
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r2.anchor: النجوم لأشياء منها أنها جعلت زينة للسماء الدنيا، ومنها أنها جعلت

TABRISI:16:15-16/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r1.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:16:15-16/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads al-najm with a ḍamma on the nūn, treating it as a plural like suquf and ruhun.

TABRISI:16:15-16/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r7.claim: A sign is a form that conveys meaning through writing, speech, gesture, or appearance; signs can be conventional or demonstrative proofs.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r7.anchor: والعلامة صورة يعلم بها المعنى من خط أو لفظ

TABRISI:16:15-16/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r10.claim: ʿAlāmāt is accusative by coordination with rivers and paths.

TABRISI:16:15-16/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:16:15-16/r11.claim: An alternative syntactic reading supplies an implied verb: God created signs for you.

TABRISI:16:15-16/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r23.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r23.claim: Signs are landmarks by which travelers learn the roads; one interpretation specifically identifies them as mountains used for daytime navigation.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r23.anchor: وجعل لكم علامات معالم تعلم بها الطرق

TABRISI:16:15-16/r24.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r24.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:16:15-16/r24.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says people use the stars for guidance at night.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r24.anchor: ليلا عن ابن عباس والمراد بالنجم الجنس

TABRISI:16:15-16/r25.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r25.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r25.claim: Al-najm is a generic singular meaning all the fixed stars.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r25.anchor: والمراد بالنجم الجنس أي جميع النجوم الثابتة

TABRISI:16:15-16/r26.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r26.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:16:15-16/r26.claim: One reading of the syntax ends the preceding sentence at ʿalāmāt and starts a new sentence with guidance by the star.

TABRISI:16:15-16/r27.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r27.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
TABRISI:16:15-16/r27.claim: Qatādah and Mujāhid say signs may themselves be stars: some guide travelers, while others are signs without guiding them.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r27.anchor: عن قتادة ومجاهد وقيل أراد به الاهتداء

TABRISI:16:15-16/r28.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r28.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:16:15-16/r28.claim: A further interpretation takes the guidance by stars to mean finding the direction of the qibla.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r28.anchor: وقيل أراد به الاهتداء في القبلة

THALABI:v6p12/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p12/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p12/r1.claim: Some take the syntax to end before this clause, which then begins a new statement.
THALABI:v6p12/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هاهنا تم الكلام ثم ابتدأ.

THALABI:v6p12/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p12/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي والكلبي
THALABI:v6p12/r2.claim: They interpret the landmarks as mountains: mountains mark the day, while stars mark the night.
THALABI:v6p12/r2.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب القرظي والكلبي: أراد بالعلامات الجبال، فالجبال علامات النهار والنجوم علامات الليل.

THALABI:v6p12/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p12/r3.speaker: مجاهد وإبراهيم
THALABI:v6p12/r3.claim: They say both terms refer to stars, some serving as landmarks and others as guides.
THALABI:v6p12/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد وإبراهيم: أراد بهما جميعا النجوم، فمنها ما يكون علامات ومنها ما يهتدون به.

THALABI:v6p12/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p12/r4.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v6p12/r4.claim: He identifies the Pleiades, Banat Naʿsh, the two Furqad stars, and al-Jadi as stars by which travelers find roads and the qibla.
THALABI:v6p12/r4.anchor: قال السدي: يعني بالثريا وبنات نعش والفرقدين والجدي فيهتدون إلى الطرق والقبلة.

THALABI:v6p12/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p12/r5.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p12/r5.claim: He says stars were created for three purposes: adornment of the sky, guidance on roads, and missiles against devils; other claims are conjecture without knowledge.
THALABI:v6p12/r5.anchor: قتادة: إنما خلق الله النجوم لثلاث أشياء: لتكون زينة للسماء، وعلامات للطريق ورجوما للشياطين.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r1.claim: The word علامات is coordinated with what precedes it; a sign is a perceptible form conveying meaning, and its root is علم.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r1.anchor: وعلامات} منسوقة (¬3) على ما قبلها، والعلامة صورة يعلم بها المعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r2.speaker: الكلبي والقرظي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r2.claim: They identify the signs as mountains, landmarks by day like the stars at night; on this reading the clause ends here, as al-Akhfash holds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r2.anchor: فقال الكلبي والقرظي: يعني الجبال (¬4)، وهي علامات للطرق بالنهار كالنجوم بالليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r3.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's transmission, the signs are the stars in the sky, but the author prefers mountains because the signs are coordinated with things created on earth and the verse then distinguishes the star.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية # عطاء: يريد نجوم السماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r4.claim: The author argues that if علامات meant stars the wording would say by them; the following mention of the star shows that the signs are something other than stars.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r4.anchor: فلما قال: {وبالنجم} دل أن المراد بالعلامات غير النجم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r5.speaker: مجاهد وإبراهيم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r5.claim: They interpret guidance by the star as guidance by all stars; al-Zajjāj chooses this, since singular نجم can have the same collective sense as its plural.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد وإبراهيم: أراد جميع النجوم (¬3)، واختاره الزجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r6.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r6.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's transmission, the star means the constellation al-Jady.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يعني الجدي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r7.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r7.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the stars as al-Thurayyā and Banāt Naʿsh.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: يعني الثريا وبنات نعش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r8.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies them as the two Firqads and al-Jady; al-Farrāʾ chooses this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r8.anchor: يعني الفرقدين والجدي (¬1)، وهو اختيار الفراء (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r9.claim: The stars guide people to roads and the direction of prayer on land and sea.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p35/r9.anchor: أي إلى الطريق والقبلة في البر والبحر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:13-16/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:13-16/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:13-16/r5.claim: The landmarks are mountains that mark routes by day, while stars guide people to routes and the direction of prayer on land and sea.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:13-16/r5.anchor: يعني الجبال، وهي علامات الطرق بالنهار { وبالنجم } يعني: جميع النجوم { هم يهتدون } إلى الطرق والقبلة في البر والبحر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r2.claim: God placed signs along people's routes so they can recognize the way.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r2.anchor: {وعلامات} [النحل: 16] جعلها في طرقهم يعرفون بها الطريق.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r3.claim: People navigate by the stars; here “the star” means the group of stars used for wayfinding.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r3.anchor: {وبالنجم هم يهتدون} [النحل: 16] ، يعني: يعرفون الطريق. والنجم: جماعة النجوم التي يهتدون بها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r4.speaker: حسان بن بلال العنزي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r4.claim: Hassan ibn Bilal warns that attributing any other function to these stars is false, sinful, slanderous, and an innovation.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r4.anchor: النضر بن معبد، عن حسان بن بلال العنزي، قال: من قال في هذه النجوم سوى هذه الثلاث فهو كاذب، آثم، مفتر، مبتدع.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r5.claim: The three functions are to serve as lamps, missiles against devils, and guides for travel, as linked to other verses.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r5.anchor: قال الله: {ولقد زينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح} [الملك: 5] ، قال: {وجعلناها رجوما للشياطين} [الملك: 5] . وقال: {وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر}

BURHAN:v1p102/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p102/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p102/r10.claim: In the statement about finding one's way by the stars, huda means knowledge.

BURHAN:v2p12/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p12/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p12/r2.claim: The formula As for me, I do not do it signals dislike, as in the Prophet's statement that he does not eat reclining.
BURHAN:v2p12/r2.anchor: وأما لفظ ( أما أنا فلا أفعل ) فالمحقق فيه الكراهة

BURHAN:v2p12/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p12/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p12/r4.claim: Permissibility can be inferred from explicit allowance, removal of blame, permission, pardon, conditional choice, mention of benefits, silence about prohibition, or approval of conduct during revelation.
BURHAN:v2p12/r4.anchor: وتستفاد الإباحة من لفظ الإحلال ورفع الجناح والإذن والعفو

BURHAN:v2p12/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p12/r5.speaker: جابر
BURHAN:v2p12/r5.claim: Jabir's report that the Companions practiced withdrawal while the Quran was being revealed exemplifies divine tacit approval; Hasan's poetry recitation before the Prophet exemplifies prophetic approval when aware.
BURHAN:v2p12/r5.anchor: فمن إقرار الرب قول جابر ( كنا نعزل والقرآن ينزل )

BURHAN:v2p12/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p12/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p12/r7.claim: Divine rebuke preceding an act indicates its prohibition; the author cites five rebukes across al-Anfal, al-Tawba, al-Ahzab, al-Tahrim, and Abasa, contrasting Ibn Abd al-Salam's treatment of rebuke as evidence for a prohibition.
BURHAN:v2p12/r7.anchor: تقديم العتاب على الفعل من الله تعالى يدل على تحريمه فقد عاتب الله سبحانه في خمسة مواضع

BURHAN:v2p12/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p12/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p12/r8.claim: One cannot claim divine favor for something forbidden; the author rejects the view that the favor is creation of an ability to endure it.
BURHAN:v2p12/r8.anchor: لا يصح الإمتنان بممنوع عنه خلافا لمن زعم أنه يصح ويصرف الإمتنان إلى خلقه للصبر عليهم

ITQAN:v2p410/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p410/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p410/r7.claim: Huda can mean knowledge, as in being guided by the stars.

DAMGHANI:v1p447/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r9.claim: Najm can mean celestial stars, which guide travelers and are also the stars observed in the cited passages.
DAMGHANI:v1p447/r9.anchor: فوجه منها : النجوم الكواكب . قوله سبحانه فى سورة الطارق

DAMGHANI:v1p472/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r9.claim: Hadā can mean knowing or recognizing; the source glosses guidance by the stars as recognition and cites two further uses of the verb.
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r9.anchor: الخامس الهدى المعرفة قوله تعالى في سورة النحل وعلامات وبالنجم هم يهتدون أي يعرفون

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r1.claim: Hudā can mean recognition or discernment, including recognizing landmarks and finding a route.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r1.anchor: والخامس : العرفان . ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r1.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r1.claim: In ordinary usage najm means a star, perhaps named for its visible appearance; exegetes give the Quranic term this sense in the guidance and stellar references.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r1.anchor: النجم : في مطلق التعارف الكوكب وجمعه نجوم . وقيل : سمي نجما لظهوره

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r4.claim: In Arabic, najm can also mean a newly appearing plant, the emerging tip of a horn or tooth, the Pleiades, or any stalkless plant.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r4.anchor: ويقال : النجم : النبت إذا ظهر . ونجم القرن والسن : إذا طلعا . والنجم من النبات : ما ليس له ساق

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.claim: Rafʿ in له علم علم الفقهاء presents knowledge and related traits as established virtues and distinguishing marks, like حلم, عقل, and فضل, rather than momentary actions.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.anchor: لأن هذه خصال تذكرها فى الرجل كالحلم والعقل والفضل

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.claim: Accusative علم علم الفقهاء instead describes someone encountered while learning, before علم is an established trait; it reports an ongoing action rather than praise for a completed quality.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.anchor: وإن شئت نصبت فقلت له علم علم الفقهاء

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.claim: The stable quality reading is supported by له شرف, له دين, and له فهم; unfinished qualities are expressed with verbs such as يتدين, يتشرف, and يتفهم.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.anchor: لأن هذه خصال تذكرها فى الرجل كالحلم والعقل والفضل

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلهعلمعلمالفقهاءولهرأىرأ.claim: With له صوت صوت حمار, the accusative describes the sound made at the time of encounter; unlike knowledge, صوت is an action rather than a settled bodily quality.

DURR-FULL:v5p119/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p119/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v5p119/r1.claim: Ibrahim saw no harm in learning enough about the stars to find one’s way by them.
DURR-FULL:v5p119/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم أنه كان لا يرى بأسا أن يتعلم الرجل من النجوم ما يهتدي به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r1.claim: The author calls a preceding explanation, not preserved in this excerpt, weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا عندي توجيه ضعيف، وقال الفراء: المراد الجدي والفرقدان.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r2.speaker: الفراء
