IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ identifies the stars under discussion as al-Jady and the two al-Farqadān stars.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r3.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r3.claim: Another view identifies the star as the Pole Star, which does not move.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r3.anchor: وقال غيره: المراد القطب الذي لا يجري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r4.claim: After mentioning other identifications, the author prefers that ‘the star’ is a generic term.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r4.anchor: وقال قوم: هو اسم الجنس وهذا هو الصواب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r1.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r1.claim: Al-Awfi transmits from Ibn Abbas that the signs are landmarks, and that people navigate by stars at night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r1.anchor: أحدها أنها معالم الطرف بالنهار وبالنجم هم يهتدون وبالليل رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r2.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والنخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r2.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Nakhaʿi say the signs are stars, some of which mark things without guiding travelers and some of which guide them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r2.anchor: والثاني أنها النجوم أيضا منها ما يكون علامة لا يهتدى به ومنها ما يهتدى به قاله مجاهد وقتادة والنخعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r3.speaker: ابن السائب ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r3.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib and Muqatil say the signs are mountains.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r3.anchor: والثالث الجبال قاله ابن السائب ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r4.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the star as a group including the Pleiades, the two Furqads, the Daughters of the Bier, and al-Jadi.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r4.anchor: أحدها أنه الثريا والفرقدان وبنات نعش والجدي قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r5.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r5.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib identifies the star as al-Jadi and the two Furqads.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r5.anchor: والثاني أنه الجدي والفرقدان قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r6.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r6.claim: Al-Mawardi identifies it as al-Jadi alone, said to be the most fixed of all stars at its center.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r6.anchor: والثالث أنه الجدي وحده لأنه أثبت النجوم كلها في مركزه ذكره الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes al-najm as a generic singular referring to all stars.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r7.anchor: والرابع أنه اسم جنس والمراد جميع النجوم قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r8.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وأبو المتوكل ويحيى بن وثاب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r8.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Abu al-Mutawakkil, and Yahya ibn Waththab read al-najm with a damma on nūn and a still jīm.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والضحاك وأبو المتوكل ويحيى بن وثاب وبالنجم بضم النون وإسكان الجيم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r9.speaker: الجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r9.claim: Al-Jahdari reads al-najm with both nūn and jīm vocalized with damma.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري وبالنجم بضم النون والجيم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r10.claim: Mujahid reads the plural al-nujūm, with a wāw.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r10.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وبالنجوم بواو على الجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r11.claim: The guidance provided by the stars is understood either as finding the direction of prayer or finding one's way while traveling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p436/r11.anchor: وفي المراد بهذا الاهتداء قولان أحدهما الاهتداء إلى القبلة والثاني إلى الطريق في السفر
